title: Keeping a knife sharp and storing it safely

items.stem: Why is a dull knife more dangerous than a sharp one when you cut a tomato?

options.text: It cuts skin worse, so cuts need longer to heal
It is lighter, so it is harder to control well
It needs more force, so it slips off more easily
It cannot cut skin, so you feel safe and relax

items.stem: You run a knife along a honing steel a few times. What does this do to the knife?

options.text: It grinds off metal to form a brand new edge
It straightens the edge that has bent over slightly
It cleans off food and oil that dulls the edge
It hardens the steel so the edge stays sharp longer

items.stem: A knife still slides off a tomato's skin after you hone it well. What does the knife now need, in one word?
Which is the safest way to clean a kitchen knife after use?

options.text: Drop it in the sink and wash it with the dishes
Soak it in hot soapy water until the food loosens
Put it in the dishwasher, loose in the cutlery basket
Wash it by hand, wiping with the edge facing away

items.stem: You have dried a clean knife. Which place is the safest to store it?

options.text: In a knife block, or on a wall magnet strip
Loose in the drawer, together with the spoons
On the counter, with the blade pointing away
In the dish rack, so that it stays dry longer

items.stem: Why should you never leave a knife soaking in a sink full of soapy water? Answer in one sentence.
